## Summary

I am a statistician and scientist with more than ten years of experience working on real
research problems in ecology, forestry, and wildfire science. My work focuses on building
statistical and machine-learning models that people can actually use to make decisions.

Much of this work involves Bayesian modeling, spatial data, and situations where data are
messy, incomplete, or structured in ways that violate standard assumptions. I spend a
large portion of my time collaborating with other scientists to design studies, choose appropriate
models, and interpret results correctly.

## What I Work On

- Statistical modeling for real decision problems  
- Quantifying uncertainty and explaining what it means in practice  
- Spatial, temporal, and multivariate data analysis  
- Forest resource and wildfire-related systems  

## Methods I Use

- Bayesian models, including hierarchical and multilevel models  
- Decision trees, random forests, and gradient boosting  
- Gaussian process and other nonlinear models  
- Study design for observational and experimental data  
- Model checking, validation, and sensitivity analysis  

## Working With Other Scientists

- Collaborating with teams to decide which models make sense for their data  
- Reviewing analyses and identifying problems before results are used  
- Mentoring researchers in statistical reasoning and modeling  
- Explaining results to people without formal statistical training  

## Education

**Ph.D., Statistics** — Virginia Tech  
**M.S., Statistics** — Virginia Tech  
**B.S., Mathematics** — University of North Carolina at Greensboro  

## Professional Experience

### USDA Forest Service — Mathematical Statistician  
**2016 – Present**

- Built statistical and machine-learning models to study wildfire-related survival outcomes,
  which have been used in policy discussions and external guidance.
- Developed probabilistic and nonlinear models to predict forest growth and support
  timber and land management decisions.
- Designed models to support ecosystem restoration, including work on forest disease
  and recovery.
- Advised more than 50 interdisciplinary research teams on study design, modeling approaches,
  and interpretation of results.
- Trained and mentored more than 100 scientists through workshops, short courses,
  and one-on-one consultation in Bayesian modeling and applied statistics.


### National Institute for Mathematical and Biological Synthesis (NIMBioS) — Postdoctoral Fellow  
**2015 – 2016**

- Developed Bayesian methods to study functional similarity in ecological systems.
- Built clustering models for complex, multi-species data.
- Worked closely with domain scientists to align statistical assumptions with biology.

### Colorado State University — Postdoctoral Fellow  
**2013 – 2015**

- Developed Bayesian correction models for high-throughput sequencing data.
- Produced spatial statistical analyses of soil microbial processes across large regions.
- Collaborated across statistics, ecology, and biogeochemistry.

### Virginia Tech — Laboratory for Interdisciplinary Statistical Analysis (LISA)  
**Lead Collaborator**  
**2008 – 2013**

- Served as the primary statistical collaborator on more than 140 research projects.
- Helped researchers design studies, analyze data, and prepare results for publication.
- Taught short courses and workshops on applied statistical methods.
